newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court delays ruling on bank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court delays ruling on bank insolvency.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Wednesday postponed for a second time its ruling on an insolvency suit filed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) against the First Private Bank (FPB), a BNB official said.

"The case is postponed until December 11 because it has been sent to the Supreme Court following an appeal filed by the FPB's former executive directors," said Borislav Stratev, head of the BNB's legal department.

The former FPB management has appealed against the Sofia court's refusal to accept it as a side in the suit because under Bulgarian law banks placed under special supervision can be represented only by the sequestrators.
The Supreme Court is expected to rule on the former management's appeal on November 25.
The BNB placed FPB, Bulgaria's biggest private bank, and state-owned Mineral Bank under special supervision in May dismissing their boards and curbing their operations. @
The BNB then appointed sequestrators to investigate the banks' coundition and requested the start of bankruptcy proceedings through the courts.
The city court also postponed its ruling in June because the sequestrators' findings on the FPB's assets to debt ratio had not been completed.

The FPB owes some 31 billion levs to the State Savings Bank and the central bank lent to it as refinancing. The bank owes a further 20 billion levs paid out by the Post Bank as compensation for individual and company deposits. @
The Sofia court is expected to rule on the insolvency suit against Mineralbank, on September 25. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
